findings.claim: The serializer method `include_website_name` lacks the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializer requires for `include_<attr>?` predicates. As a result it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, as null when there is no website.

verifier.reason: UserSerializer inherits from ActiveModel::Serializer and declares :website_name at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43, but defines include_website_name without the trailing '?' at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153-155. Because ActiveModel::Serializer only checks include_<attr>? predicates, this method is never called and website_name is always serialized, returning nil (JSON null) at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 when there is no website.

findings.claim: UserSerializer's `website_name` does not honor `Guardian#restrict_user_fields?` and is not in `untrusted_attributes`, unlike `website`. This exposes the website host/path of TL0 users to anonymous viewers.

verifier.reason: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 and app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:105-111, `:website_name` is serialized as an attribute but omitted from `untrusted_attributes` (unlike `:website`), and neither `website_name` nor `include_website_name` (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:137-155, which also lacks a trailing `?`) checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result, TL0 users' website host/path is still exposed to anonymous viewers despite `UserGuardian#restrict_user_fields?` (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60), and is even rendered on the profile page (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:69-76).
